test.title: Electrostatics - Test 5
test.description: Previous Year Questions as Chapter Test
test.syllabus: This test contains questions from all topics of this chapter included in the JEE Main syllabus. It includes a mix of questions from PYQs of JEE Main 2019 - 2025.

question.text: Charge is distributed within a sphere of radius <math><mi>R</mi></math> with a volume charge density <math><mi>ρ</mi><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>A</mi></mrow><mrow><msup><mrow><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfrac><msup><mrow><mi>e</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>r</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow></mfrac></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> where <math><mi>A</mi></math> and <math><mi>a</mi></math> are constants. If <math><mi>Q</mi></math> is the total charge of this charge distribution, the radius <math><mi>R</mi></math> is:
A point charge +q is placed at the origin. A second point charge +9 q is placed at $(\mathrm{d}, 0,0)$ in Cartesian coordinate system. The point in between them where the electric field vanishes is :
The electrostatic potential due to an electric dipole at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> varies as :

Shown in the figure is a shell made of a conductor. It has inner radius a and outer radius b, and carries charge Q . At its centre a dipole p→ is placed as shown then:

options.text: Surface charge density on the inner surface of the shell is zero everywhere.
Electric field outside the shell is the same as that of a point charge at the centre of the shell.

Surface charge density on the inner surface is uniform and equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mrow><mo>(</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mi>Q</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mstyle><mo>)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">π</mi><msup><mi>a</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mfrac></math>.

Surface charge density on the outer surface depends on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="|" close="|" separators="|"><mover accent="true"><mi>p</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math>

question.text: Consider the force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math> on a charge '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></math>' due to a uniformly charged spherical shell of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">R</mi></math> carrying charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">Q</mi></math> distributed uniformly over it. Which one of the following statements is true for <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">F</mi></math>, if  '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">q</mi></math>' is placed at distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi></math> from the centre of the shell?

.

An infinitely long wire has uniform linear charge density $\lambda=2 \mathrm{nC} / \mathrm{m}$. The net flux through a Gaussian cube of side length $\sqrt{3} \mathrm{~cm}$, if the wire passes through any two corners of the cube, that are maximally displaced from each other, would be $\mathrm{xNm}^2 \mathrm{C}^{-1}$, where x is :
[Neglect any edge effects and use $\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0}=9 \times 10^9$ SI units]

A positive charge particle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mg</mi></math> is thrown in opposite direction to a uniform electric field of strength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the charge on the particle is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> and the initial velocity is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, how much distance it will travel before coming to the rest momentarily

If coordinates of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> respectively, the work done by electric field will be

A line charge of length $\frac{\text { ' } a \text { ' }}{2}$ is kept at the center of an edge $B C$ of a cube $A B C D E F G H$ having edge length ' $a$ ' as shown in the figure. If the density of line charge is $\lambda$ C per unit length, then the total electric flux through all the faces of the cube will be _______. (Take, $\epsilon_0$ as the free space permittivity)

Two identical conducting spheres $P$ and $S$ with charge $Q$ on each, repel each other with a force $16 \mathrm{~N}$. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere $R$ is successively brought in contact with the two spheres. The new force of repulsion between $\mathrm{P}$ and $\mathrm{S}$ is :
An electric dipole is placed at a distance of 2 cm from an infinite plane sheet having positive charge density $\sigma_{\mathrm{o}}$. Choose the correct option from the following.

options.text: Potential energy and torque both are maximum.
Torque on dipole is zero and net force is directed away from the sheet.
Torque on dipole is zero and net force acts towards the sheet.
Potential energy of dipole is minimum and torque is zero.

question.text: Figure shows a rod AB, which is bent in a 120° circular arc of radius R. A charge (-Q) is uniformly distributed over rod AB. What is the electric filed E→ at the centre of curvature O ?

Ten charges are placed on the circumference of a circle of radius R with constant angular separation between successive charges. Alternate charges<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn></math> have charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo></math> each, while <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>10</mn></math> have charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mo>–</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo></math> each. The potential V and the electric field E at the centre of the circle are respectively : (Take<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> at infinity)

Two isolated metallic solid spheres of radii <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>R</mi></math> are charged such that both have same charge density <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>σ</mi></math> . The spheres are then connected by a thin conducting wire. If the new charge density of the bigger sphere is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup></math>. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>σ</mi><mo>'</mo></msup><mi>σ</mi></mfrac></math> is :

A point particle of charge $Q$ is located at $P$ along the axis of an electric dipole 1 at a distance $r$ as shown in the figure. The point P is also on the equatorial plane of a second electric dipole 2 at a distance r . The dipoles are made of opposite charge q separated by a distance $2 a$. For the charge particle at P not to experience any net force, which of the following correctly describes the situation?

Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R)
Assertion (A) : Work done by electric field on moving a positive charge on an equipotential surface is always zero.
Reason (R) : Electric lines of forces are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

question.text: An electric field, $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{E}}=\frac{2 \hat{i}+6 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}}$ passes through the surface of $4 \mathrm{~m}^2$ area having unit vector $\hat{n}=\left(\frac{2 \hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{6}}\right)$. The electric flux for that surface is ______ $\mathrm{Vm}$.
